response.title: which dehumidifier removes the most water in a cold basement
response.answer:
For a cold basement, the dehumidifier that removes the most water isn't necessarily the one with the highest advertised pint rating.

Most conventional dehumidifiers are rated at 65°F (18°C) and 60% relative humidity. When your basement drops to 40–50°F (4–10°C), their water-removal capacity can fall dramatically.

There are two main choices:

Low-temperature refrigerant dehumidifiers: Best for basements that stay around 50–60°F. High-capacity commercial models can remove substantial amounts of water.

Desiccant dehumidifiers: Often better below 45–50°F, because they don't depend on cooling coils that can freeze.

If your priority is maximum water removal, I'd look at commercial models rather than ordinary 35- or 50-pint household units.
